content.text:
# The one shared reverse proxy. Instance-agnostic: it is started once and then attached to each
# instance network with `docker network connect --alias`, so inside every instance network it
# answers to that instance's public *.localhost names. That is what makes the Keycloak issuer
# the browser sees identical to the one the backend validates.
#
# The container must listen on the same port it publishes: the generated per-instance nginx confs
# (scripts/urbo/render.mjs) `listen ${URBO_PROXY_PORT}`, so a container that always answered on 80
# internally would silently go dark the moment URBO_PROXY_PORT picked anything else — the escape
# hatch for a taken port 80 would advertise a working URL that never actually connects.
services:
  urbo-proxy:
    container_name: urbo-proxy
    image: nginx:alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Dev-server blocks rendered by scripts/urbo use only the IPv4 entry this writes (see proxy.mjs's
    # hostGatewayIpv4). Confs installed by older checkouts still name host.docker.internal.
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"
    ports:
      - "${URBO_PROXY_PORT:-80}:${URBO_PROXY_PORT:-80}"
    volumes:
      - urbo-proxy-conf:/etc/nginx/conf.d

volumes:
  urbo-proxy-conf:
